The CLI and skills are built on branch `orca-cli-skills` and pass the new test (9/9). They are not merged or switched yet: two read-only reviewers are still running over the change.

**What it adds (in `orca.nix`):**
- **`orca` CLI:** runs Orca's own CLI script inside the same sandboxed environment as the app, so it works from any shell, not just Orca's terminals. The app keeps its existing `orca-ide` command.
- **6 skills in `~/.claude/skills`:** orca-cli, orchestration, computer-use, orca-per-workspace-env, orca-linear, linear-tickets. They come from the exact commit this Orca version was built from. All six are short files that point the agent at `orca skills get`, which is why the CLI has to work everywhere.
- **`tests/orca-cli-skills.sh`:** checks that `orca` runs with every Orca variable removed and the in-Orca `orca` shortcut taken off `PATH`. It also checks each skill against the fingerprints that ship inside the app, so a version bump that forgets to update the skills commit fails the test.

**Checks I ran:**
- `orca status`, run with all Orca variables removed, reached the running app.
- The full shiori home config still builds without errors.

- **Review:** drovr's usual review command needs a herdr pane, and this session runs inside Orca, so it exited before reviewing anything. I started two read-only reviewer agents over the same changes instead (correctness/error handling, and security/quality).
- **Leftover link:** the app had already put its own link at `~/.local/bin/orca-ide`, pointing at an exact store path. It will break once that path is garbage-collected after a version bump. I didn't touch it.

**Next (~2 min, after the reviews come back and I fix anything they find):** I merge to master and run `hms`. Then try it from any terminal outside Orca with `orca skills list`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
# that `orca` runs from any shell, not only an Orca terminal, and that the
# skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
#
# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, which outside the FHS env is
# an Electron binary looking for the host's libraries. The skills are stubs
# that tell the agent to run `orca skills get <name>`, so a skill without a
# working CLI is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a commit separately
# from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other silently installs
# guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes in
# resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are held to.
#
# Usage:
#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it

set -u
set -o pipefail

fails=0; n=0
pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }

FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
# uname -n, not /etc/hostname: Orca's sandbox does not bind the latter in.
HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(uname -n).config"
SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"

drv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
  --apply 'ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or "") == "orca-cli") ps)).drvPath') \
  || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "testing $CLI"

if [ -x "$CLI/bin/orca" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/orca"
else fail "bin/orca" "missing from $CLI"; fi

# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's runScript
# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
manifest=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
  f="$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"; [ -f "$f" ] && echo "$f"; done | head -1)
[ -n "$manifest" ] || { echo "no skills manifest in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }

# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
outside() { env $(env | grep -o '^ORCA_[A-Z_]*' | sed 's/^/-u /') PATH="$clean_path" "$@"; }

want_version=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
  --apply 'ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or "") == "orca-cli") ps)).version')
got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi

# `skills list` reads the bundled guide table locally, no running app needed.
got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" skills list --json 2>&1)
if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '"orca-cli"'; then pass "orca skills list works outside Orca"
else fail "orca skills list" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi

The first review round found that the installed skills tell agents outside Orca to run `orca-ide`, which was the GUI. That's fixed, and both tests pass (`tests/orca-cli-skills.sh` 15/15, `tests/sandbox-fonts.sh` 5/5). A second review round is still running, so nothing is merged or switched yet.

**Fixes from review round 1:**
- **`orca-ide` is now the CLI**, as you chose, and `orca` is the same CLI. The GUI command is `orca-ide-app`, and the desktop entry launches that.
- **`orca-ide open`** starts the GUI through its normal wrapper, so it gets the Wayland flag, fonts and GPU setup. Without this it would have started bare Electron, which exits on Hyprland.
- **The test is now stricter:**
  - It checks that the CLI runs in a sandbox of its own. Run from an Orca terminal, the old test would also have passed a bare wrapper that only works there.
  - It runs `skills get` under both names, since that is the command every skill uses.
  - It checks that the skills commit matches the commit Orca records inside the app. A version bump that forgets the skills commit now fails.
- **Comments in `orca.nix`** explain why only 6 of the 10 skills are installed. They also note that Orca's own **Settings → Skills → update** will fail or clobber these read-only links, so update them by bumping the pin in `orca.nix` instead.

Your habit changes: plain `orca-ide` no longer opens the app. Use `orca-ide-app`, the desktop entry, or `orca-ide open`.

Both commits are on branch `orca-cli-skills`: `9e53e6cc` and `777a68b5`.

**Next:** I need two review rounds in a row with no blocking findings. If round 2 is clean, round 3 runs on the same code. Then I merge to master and run `hms`, about 10–15 minutes. After that, try `orca-ide skills get orca-cli` in a terminal outside Orca.

- Separately, nothing actually runs `orca open`. The "honours this override and strips ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE" claim is true in upstream code (`out/cli/runtime/launch.js` and `orca-app-executable.js` read `ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE` and call `stripElectronRunAsNode`), but the test only checks it statically. Acceptable if intended; the pass message overstates it.

### Nits

- **orca.nix:100-101:** "`orca` (what they run inside one…)". Inside an Orca terminal, `~/.config/orca/linux-orca-cli-shim/orca` comes before `~/.nix-profile/bin` on PATH, so the shim wins and this package's `orca` only serves "elsewhere". Wording overclaims slightly.
- **orca.nix:156-159:** the whole skill directory is a store symlink. home.nix:2176-2185 links skills file by file (`…/SKILL.md`). The comment at 136-139 justifies the choice, so this is a style difference only. No clobber conflict exists today: `~/.claude/skills` has none of the six.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:30:** `SKILLS` copies `orcaSkills` from orca.nix. Removing a skill from orca.nix fails the test (good). Adding one, or the home.file set growing, is not checked. Deriving the list via `nix eval … home.file --apply 'attrNames'` filtered on `.claude/skills/` would close that.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:58:** `grep -q bwrap` matches any mention of "bwrap", including the launcher's own comment text ("mounting one via bwrap", line 117 of the launcher). A tighter match is `grep -qE '/bin/bwrap$'` or `exec "\$\{cmd`.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:88:** `grep -q '^# '` accepts any markdown heading. Comparing against the SKILL.md / bundled-guide title would be stricter. Low risk.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:94-108:** only SKILL.md is hashed. That matches today's manifest (every one of the ten entries lists only `SKILL.md`), but a skill that later gains files would be partly checked. Iterating `files[]` would avoid that. The exit status of `nix-store --realise "$srcdrv"` (line 101) is ignored, but the hash check still catches a failed fetch ("missing"), so no false pass.
- **orca.nix:95-98 vs 7-93:** comment density and style match the existing blocks (why-first, measured claims, cross-references to tests). No issue.

### Verified as accurate
- **"defaultFhsEnvArgs already carries libsecret" (orca.nix:108-109):** true. In nixpkgs `pkgs/build-support/appimage/default.nix:112-131`, `defaultFhsEnvArgs.targetPkgs` includes `libsecret`.
- **"wrapType2 pins runScript to AppRun" (orca.nix:107):** true in effect. wrapAppImage sets `runScript = "appimage-exec.sh -w ${contents} --"` (line 77), which runs AppRun.
- **"rev in the store name so a rev-only bump fails" (orca.nix:131-133):** true. fetchFromGitHub's default name is `repoRevToNameMaybe …`, and with the default `config.fetchedSourceNameDefault = "source"` (top-level/config.nix:97-103) that is just `source`. A fixed-output path depends only on name and hash, so without the rev in the name a rev bump would reuse the old tree. With it, the path changes and the hash mismatch fails the fetch.
- **"A subset of the bundled ten: no Jira, no emulator" (orca.nix:136):** the manifest lists exactly ten. The four left out are jira-tickets, orca-jira, orca-emulator and orca-emulator-android.
- **The rev regex (test:98)** matches the real path `/nix/store/g2wc6v5x…-orca-skills-e6f7fba58e8e47b45e4343f99101b3ca9e05a5da/skills/orca-cli`. A regression that drops the rev from `name` makes it fail as "unparsed", which is good.
- **The `sourceCommit` literal (test:99):** app.asar contains `` sourceCommit:`e6f7fba58e8e47b45e4343f99101b3ca9e05a5da` ``, the same rev.
- **The ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE parse (test:64):** the launcher has `--setenv ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE /nix/store/zhk2…-orca-1.4.238/bin/orca-ide-app` on one line, so the grep plus `awk '{print $3}'` is fine. The shim dir name `linux-orca-cli-shim` (test:78) matches upstream and the real PATH.
- **Runtime behaviour of a detached `orca open`:** buildFHSEnv uses `--die-with-parent` without `--unshare-pid`. container-init execs `/init` and the runScript, so a detached GUI is a grandchild and is not killed when the CLI exits.
- **Secrets:** nothing prints values. `compgen -e` is a bash builtin (the shebang is bash), and with `grep '^ORCA_'` it yields names only, which become `env -u NAME` arguments. Word splitting is safe for env names, and with no matches `env` simply runs `PATH=… cmd`. `ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_TOKEN` is unset for the child and never echoed. Failure messages print only CLI output (`--version`, the first 3 lines of `skills get`) and `ls` of the GUI bin.
- **Security:** the skills fetch is pinned by both rev and hash; the CLI and GUI are store paths; no secrets or email addresses appear in the diff. Installing upstream's computer-use skill globally into `~/.claude/skills` is a trust decision, not a defect.
- **tests/sandbox-fonts.sh:25:** the usage line rename to `orca-ide-app` is correct. Its `.*orca-[0-9.]+` filter (line 38) still selects the GUI and not `orca-cli-1.4.238`.

Fix items 1 and 2 before running the test through `hmeval --ci`. Item 3 is a one-line tightening.

    - Point ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE at a wrapper that adds the flag only when `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is unset.

  - No case covers finding 1. One that runs `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$app" -e 0` and expects exit 0 would catch it.

Round 2 found 5 Important issues; all are fixed and committed. Round 3 of review is running over the full branch. `tests/orca-cli-skills.sh` passes 16/16 and `tests/sandbox-fonts.sh` 5/5.

**Fixed in round 2 (commit `4e0f5355`):**
1. **`orca-ide serve`:** it runs the GUI command in node mode, and the always-on Wayland flag made node reject it (exit 9). The GUI wrapper now adds `--ozone-platform=wayland` only outside node mode, and a new test case covers this.
2. **Tests in CI:** both orca tests now read `/etc/hostname` (what CI writes) and fall back to `uname -n` inside Orca. The manifest check uses `jq` instead of `python3`, which CI doesn't have, and hashes every file each skill lists.
3. **`orca-ide open` check:** the test now requires exactly the nixGL-wrapped GUI. It used to pass for the unwrapped one too.

**Kept as-is (nits):**
- Bare `orca` stays in the profile. The skills warn it can be the GNOME screen reader, but that isn't installed here.
- The test keeps its own list of the six skills, so removing one from `orca.nix` fails it.

**Your call:** the app's own `~/.local/bin/orca-ide` link still exists and points at an exact store path. Nix's `orca-ide` comes first on `PATH` in Orca terminals, which is the only order I checked. That link will break once the old store path is cleaned up after a version bump. I'd delete it, but it's your file, so I haven't. To remove it: `! rm ~/.local/bin/orca-ide`

**Next:** if round 3 has no blocking findings, a round 4 runs on the same code. Two clean rounds in a row, then I merge to master and run `hms` (about 10–15 minutes).

  ## Round 3 review: `2f5d3162..HEAD` (orca.nix, tests/orca-cli-skills.sh, tests/sandbox-fonts.sh)
  
  The round-2 fix for node mode is correct. The round-1 fix (`ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE`) has a lifetime bug that no test covers. I checked what I could without starting the GUI: the built wrappers, the app's CLI JS, one bwrap experiment, and the test's eval and jq steps run against the shiori build. I did not run the full test script or `orca-ide open`.
  
  ### Critical
  
  **C1. orca.nix:25 and orca.nix:129: a GUI started by `orca-ide open` is SIGKILLed when the CLI exits.**
  - `wrapType2` defaults to `dieWithParent = true`. The GUI's bwrap launcher (`/nix/store/dhcdkbcg…-orca-1.4.238-bwrap`, line 101) contains `--die-with-parent`.
  - `launchOrcaApp()` (out/cli/runtime/launch.js:43-50) spawns `ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE` with `detached: true`. Each layer in between `exec`s the next: outer nixGL `exec -a`, then `nixGLCombinedWrapper`, then `nixGLIntel`, then the inner `orca-ide-app`, then `exec "${cmd[@]}"`. So the GUI's bwrap ends up as a direct child of the CLI's node process.
  - `openOrca()` (client.js:214-238) returns once the window is "available", or after its 15s timeout. The CLI then exits, and bwrap's parent-death signal kills the whole GUI sandbox. `setsid`/`detached` does not stop this.
  - I reproduced it with the same bwrap binary:
    - `bash -c "setsid bwrap --dev-bind / / --die-with-parent sleep 57 & sleep 1"` leaves the sleep dead once bash exits.
    - The same command without `--die-with-parent` survives.
  - Impact: the `orca-cli` and `orchestration` skills (SKILL.md:43 and :62) tell agents to run `ORCA open --json` when Orca is not running. With this setup the window appears, then dies when the command returns. The agent's next command fails with "not running" again.
  - `serve` is not affected, because it stays alive as the parent.
  - Fix: add `dieWithParent = false;` to the `wrapType2` args (buildFHSEnv supports it at build-fhsenv-bubblewrap/default.nix:48). Also add a test case: grep the GUI launcher for no `--die-with-parent`, or launch a stub in the same way.
  
  ### Important
  
  None found that the round-2 changes introduced.
  
  What I verified:
  - **Heredoc escaping renders a correct script.** The built `/nix/store/sz6x7f1zq47ng1am50460a9hi4rjd37f-orca-1.4.238/bin/orca-ide-app` (checked with `cat -A`) has:
    - the shebang at column 0;
    - `if [ -n "${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE:-}" ]`;
    - `"$@"` in both branches;
    - `$out` expanded at build time.
    
    `\''${` becomes `\${` in Nix, and the unquoted heredoc turns that into `${`.
  - **The `-n` test is right.** The app always passes the string `'1'` (serve-orcad-launch.js:35). Electron enters node mode for any non-empty value, so `-n` matches its behaviour, including `"0"`.
  - **Node mode works end to end.** `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app -e …` exits 0, going through nixGL, bwrap and AppRun. Adding `--ozone-platform=wayland` gives exit 9, so the new test case catches a regression.
  - **AppRun's `--no-sandbox` injection is still a latent risk (unchanged, environment-dependent).** In node mode, `--no-sandbox` also gives "bad option", exit 9 (reproduced). AppRun adds it whenever `unshare -Ur true` fails inside the GUI's bwrap. In the real `serve` path the GUI bwrap is nested inside the CLI's bwrap. Nested user namespaces work on this kernel: `unshare` succeeded here, inside an existing userns. So it does not fire on Arch today, but it would on a host where nested `unshare` fails. The test runs the probe from a plain shell, not from inside the CLI env, so it would not see that case. Treat it as a known limitation, or note it in the orca.nix:50-58 comment.
  - **The CLI does not add `--no-sandbox` itself.** `getExecutableAppArgs` only does that when `dirname(executable)/AppRun` exists, and `$GUI/bin` has no AppRun.
  - **Electron `serve` still runs on X11.** It appends `--ozone-platform=x11` after the wrapper's wayland flag, and the last switch wins, as upstream intends.
  
  ### Test and CI correctness (checked; no blocking issues)
  
  - **Tools:** CI's tool shell (`.forgejo/workflows/nix-eval.yml`) has bash, coreutils, grep, sed, gawk, git, jq and diffutils. That covers `sha256sum`, `paste`, `tr`, `awk`, `jq` and `readlink`. `compgen` is a bash builtin. The image supplies `nix` and `nix-store`.
  - **Hostname:** CI writes `/etc/hostname` with `printf '%s'`, which the test's `cat` reads. Inside this sandbox `/etc/hostname` does not exist, and the `uname -n` fallback gave `shiori`.
  - **Package lookup:** the GUI is found by `pname == "orca"`, which resolves to the nixGL-wrapped `df1j…-orca-1.4.238`. Its `bin/` has only `orca-ide-app` (plus the hidden `.orca-ide-unwrapped` symlink).
  - **The `ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE` grep** matches line 131 of the CLI bwrap script exactly: `…df1j…/bin/orca-ide-app`.
  - **The `getContext` expression** yields the fetch's `.drv`. The `sourceCommit` grep matches app.asar once.
  - **The jq filter** matches the manifest schema (`.skills[].files[].{exactSha256,path}`). Each of the six skills lists one file (SKILL.md). A failed `cd` and a hash mismatch both reach `fail`.
  - **In CI**, the node probe and the CLI run as root in a privileged container. AppRun's `unshare -Ur` succeeds as root there, so I expect no false failures, though I did not run the test in CI.
  - **sandbox-fonts.sh:** the hostname fallback is fine. Its `.*orca-[0-9.]+` name match does not pick up `orca-cli-1.4.238`.
  
  ### Nits
  
  - **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:30** (same in tests/sandbox-fonts.sh:37): an empty or whitespace-only `/etc/hostname` makes `cat` succeed with an empty value, so `uname -n` is never tried. Something like `h=$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null); ${h:-$(uname -n)}` would handle it.
  - **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:113-117:** only files the manifest lists are checked. An extra file added to a skill directory upstream would install without failing the test, since `home.file` links the whole directory. Comparing the directory's file list with the manifest's would close that gap.
  - **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:111:** a failed `nix-store --realise "$srcdrv"` is silent. It later shows up as "$src is missing", which hides the real cause; adding `|| fail …` would make it clearer.
  - **orca.nix:118-123:** the comment says `orca-ide open` launches the profile's GUI but says nothing about its lifetime. Update it together with C1.
  
</agent-message>

- On the usual dev setup (run from an Orca terminal, Orca already running), Electron's single-instance lock makes that second instance quit with status 0, so the case passes. With no Orca running, the case hangs, because nothing in the test has a timeout.

**2. A second way into node mode that the wrapper does not cover** (orca.nix:52-58 comment, :61-67 wrapper)

- In node mode, Node rejects `--no-sandbox` the same way it rejects the ozone flag, so on such a host the probe breaks with the same symptom.
- Upstream's `resources/bin/orca-ide` avoids this by exec'ing `$APP_DIR/orca-ide` directly. Ours goes through AppRun.

**4. Stale comment on appimageContents** (orca.nix:97)
- It says it is "shared by the wrapper's extraInstallCommands below".

- It says the `~/.local/bin/orca-ide` symlink "is an Electron binary".

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
orca: the GUI outlives the `orca-ide open` that starts it

Review round 3 (Critical). wrapType2 defaults to --die-with-parent, and
every wrapper layer execs the next, so a GUI that `orca-ide open` spawns
detached is a bwrap whose parent is the CLI -- SIGKILLed the moment
`open` returns. dieWithParent = false; a test case holds the launcher
to it.

The node-mode case now checks printed output under a timeout: with the
env var lost on the way it would be a GUI launch, which a running
Orca's single-instance lock answers with exit 0. Comment fixes: AppRun's
--no-sandbox in node mode, appimageContents' users, the header's
description of Orca's own ~/.local/bin symlink. --version matches whole
words.

Not changed (nits): the test's skill list duplicates orcaSkills, so an
addition is not checked; files a skill dir has beyond its manifest are
not flagged; a failed fetch realise shows up as "missing"; README's
test list; an empty /etc/hostname skips the uname -n fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline origin/master..HEAD | head -1
